gaps.term: rounding errors change output by at most the change
gaps.quote: rounding errors in the operands change the output by at most the size of the change
gaps.note: Missing hypothesis. Only the bound ||M_r(f,g)|| <= ||f|| ||g|| is derived on the page; it gives ||M_r(f,g)-M_r(f',g)|| <= ||f-f'|| ||g||, which is at most ||f-f'|| only if the other operand has norm at most 1 (a disk array). Paper lines 3385-3390: 'If the other operand is a disk array, replacing one operand changes the output by at most the norm distance between its two values.' The page states it for arbitrary operands.

gaps.quote: Convolution sums over all index tuples, and the index wraps independently on each axis.
gaps.note: Inconsistent with the next sentences. The page says the index tuple runs over all d axes including the last one with t_d=r, yet also says each entry is a polynomial in the ring and M, the number of cyclic addresses, uses only the first d-1 axes. In the paper (lines 3371-3383, 4321-4327) the ring-valued array is indexed by the d-1 cyclic axes only, and the last axis of length r is the polynomial coefficient axis inside each ring entry; M_r convolves only the first d-1 axes over the ring, and the negacyclic wrap on y^r replaces the cyclic wrap on the last axis. Summing over all d index tuples with polynomial entries would double count the last axis. The reader cannot tell which description is meant.
